sessions.title: How recursion returns
turns: I can follow the calls down. What happens on the way back?

The first call waits at the line that made the recursive call. Its own local variables stay where they are. When the second call returns, the first one resumes on the next line.

Before we trace it, where would a print after the recursive call show up?
I'm confused about why the last print comes out first.
Imagine countdown(2) calls countdown(1), which calls countdown(0). The base case returns at 0. The waiting call for 1 can now print 1, then return so the call for 2 can print 2.
That makes sense. The innermost call finishes first, then each waiting call resumes.
Exactly. Try applying the same idea to a folder tree: when can the parent finish?

Start with a short countdown. Once you can trace the return order, apply the same idea to a folder tree.

sessions.title: Recursion in folder trees
turns: What if a folder has two subfolders?
Finish the first subfolder before visiting the second. A folder with no subfolders can return after visiting its files.
Got it. The parent is waiting while we finish one subtree.
Try sketching the order in which each folder returns.

sessions.title: Combinatorics: counting paths
turns: How many ways can I get to the far corner with two right steps and one up step?
List where the up step can go. Which choices give you a different order?
That helped. There are three positions for the up step.
Right. You can use the same approach for longer paths with only one up step.
